scope: User-supplied retail Xbox 360 BBX corpus used externally; no proprietary game payloads are bundled in the toolkit.

families.method: native GMX -> editable fixed-layout document -> native GMX with the original file as template
native TEX -> PNG -> native TEX with the original TEX as layout template
native DAT -> parsed command records -> native DAT
families.corpus: all .dat entries extracted from retail generator.bin

families.method: native MAP -> lossless editable row-grid document -> native MAP
families.corpus: 330 .map entries from generator.bin plus 64 level maps from map.bin

families.method: native ANM -> parsed records -> native ANM
Bmap/Xmap/map4/map5 -> editable 0x118-record document -> native table using original template
families.corpus: all matching entries extracted from retail stage.bin

families.method: wall/Xwall records -> editable name/value records -> native 20-byte table
families.corpus: all matching wall/Xwall entries extracted from retail stage.bin

families.method: native COL -> PNG -> native COL with original header template
families.corpus: all 153 .col entries extracted from retail wall.bin; 78,643,200 collision pixels total
families.coverage: both observed layouts/variants: 512x256 variant 1 (4 files) and 512x1024 variant 4 (149 files)

families.method: native XOR-obfuscated CRP -> decrypted TEX -> PNG -> rebuilt TEX -> XOR-obfuscated CRP
retail text.bin -> readable CSV -> native BBX
retail message.bin -> six readable language scripts -> native BBX

evidence_boundaries: These are no-edit byte-identity tests. They prove lossless round-trip behavior for the tested corpus, not that every arbitrary edited value is accepted by the retail runtime.
GMX remains fixed-layout/template-preserving; arbitrary topology/count/chunk-graph synthesis is not claimed.
No retail game bytes are included in this validation JSON; only derived counts, names, and methodological statements are retained.
